title: Defensive exchanges

D0.outcome: Explains that a defender trades the attacker's best pieces and relieves a cramp by exchanging.

D1.outcome: Given an attack, picks the trade that removes its most dangerous piece.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, chooses between trading, counter-attacking and holding, and avoids trades that remove his own defenders.

D3.outcome: Predicts which trade leaves the king bare and which kills the attack.

sources: sources/sheets/capablanca_chess-fundamentals.md §4 CI-42 (fewer pieces help the cramped side)
conditions: The trade removes an attacker that cannot be replaced, and does not strip a defender.
contrasts: A trade that removes the last defender near the king.
A trade that frees the attacker's remaining pieces.
A trade that changes nothing about the attack.
note: Few sheet sources; conditions mainly from CAP CI-42 and EML 4.15.
